scholarships.title: Japan Africa Dream Scholarship (JADS) Program
scholarships.official_source: African Development Bank Group, with the Government of Japan

existing.description: The Japan Africa Dream Scholarship (JADS) is a capacity building programme of the African Development Bank and the Government of Japan that offers high-achieving African students a two-year scholarship to pursue post-graduate study at master's level in energy, agriculture, health, environmental sustainability and engineering. AfDB states it covers tuition for the 24-month study programme, a monthly living stipend, air travel between the scholar's home country and the host university at the start and end of the scholarship period, and health insurance usually obtained through the university, plus an additional six months for advance preparatory study or internships after graduation. It is not complete funding in AfDB's own terms: the Bank publishes an explicit exclusion list covering visa application costs, family members, extra-curricular courses, additional travel during the study programme, supplementary educational materials, field trips, workshops, seminars, internships and educational equipment such as computers. AfDB publishes no stipend figure and no central call date, so the amount and the closing date must both be confirmed with the chosen partner university and the JADS Secretariat.
eligibility: Should have a minimum of a Bachelor's degree or its equivalent in energy, agriculture, health, environmental sustainability, engineering studies or related areas; and have excellent academic records and relevant professional experience, and a history of supporting their countries' development efforts.

Applicants should have at least 1 year of paid employment in their home country or in other African countries after receiving their Bachelors (or equivalent university) degree within the past 3 years.
Candidates should be 35 years old or younger, and in good health.

Candidates should gain admission to an approved master's degree course at a Japanese or African partner university - application for admission to be done directly through the partner universities (Refer to list of universities and approved courses).
Candidates should not be enrolled in another graduate degree programs - the program does not support applicants who are already enrolled in graduate degree programs.
Must be a citizen of one of the African Development Bank's regional member countries.

Applicants must not be an Executive Director, his/her alternate, and/or staff of all types of appointments of the African Development Bank Group or a close relative of the aforementioned by blood or adoption with the term "close relative" defined as: Mother, Father, Sister, Half-sister, Brother, Half-brother, Son, Daughter, Aunt, Uncle, Niece, or Nephew.

Note published on the AfDB eligibility page: "All eligibility criteria are strictly adhered to unless otherwise communicated. Eligibility criteria will not change during an open call for applications. However, this information is subject to change between the close of one application process and the opening of the next."
existing.eligibility_summary: Must be 35 or younger, in good health, a citizen of an African Development Bank regional member country, hold a relevant bachelor's degree with an excellent academic record plus at least one year of paid employment earned within the past three years, and secure admission to an approved master's course at a JADS partner university.
benefits: Economy class air travel between a recipient's home country and the host university at the start of the study program and immediately following the end of the scholarship period
Tuition for a graduate program and the cost of basic medical insurance, usually obtained through the university
A monthly subsistence allowance to cover living expenses, including books
For scholars engaged in research, a special grant may be available for research and thesis preparation
In special circumstances, computer literacy, preparatory language and other similar courses may be covered under the scholarship
coverage: Tuition fee coverage for the duration of the study program (24 months)
Monthly living stipend for the duration of the study program (24 months)
Air travel from the home country to the host university at the start of the study program and back home at the end of the scholarship period
Health insurance, usually obtained through the university
Additional six (6) months for advance preparatory study or internships after graduation
For scholars engaged in research, a special grant may be available for research and thesis preparation
In special circumstances, computer literacy, preparatory language and other similar courses may be covered under the scholarship
requirements: All applications should go through the partner universities, no separate application to the African Development Bank is necessary.
Only candidates who have been offered admission and endorsed by the university will be considered for the JADS Program.

Admission by the JADS partner university does not mean that you have been accepted for scholarship support; you should not take any action with respect to your current employment or otherwise, until you have been informed by the African Development Bank that you have been awarded the scholarship.
Request information and application forms and procedures from the chosen JADS partner university using the provided contacts.
The candidate completes and submits application for admission.
The university evaluates and selects applicants and gives them a provisional offer letter.

University sends list of selected candidates to the African Development Bank and the Bank further shares the list with the JADS Program Implementation Unit (PIU) to evaluate the applications based on a set criteria.
After the evaluation, the African Development Bank contacts the successful candidates and informs the universities.
Read information posted on the JADS website and review eligibility criteria carefully.

Begin gathering required documentation for the scholarship application, including: your current curriculum vitae, proof of employment for each record of employment since earning a Bachelor's degree, and certified copy of the certificate of your most advanced university degree earned.
Prepare your research plan and proposal.
Take TOEFL iBT, TOEC test for English proficiency.
documents: Proof of employment for each record of employment since earning a Bachelor's degree
Certified copy of the certificate of your most advanced university degree earned
Two professional references (identified by the applicant)
existing.english_requirement: AfDB publishes: "Take TOEFL iBT, TOEC test for English proficiency." No score minimum, test-sitting date rule or accepted-validity period is published on the JADS pages.
application_method: Request information and application forms and procedures from the chosen JADS partner university using the provided contacts.
The candidate completes and submits application for admission.
The university evaluates and selects applicants and gives them a provisional offer letter.

University sends list of selected candidates to the African Development Bank and the Bank further shares the list with the JADS Program Implementation Unit (PIU) to evaluate the applications based on a set criteria.
After the evaluation, the African Development Bank contacts the successful candidates and informs the universities.
existing.selection_notes: All eligible applications are comparatively evaluated by the Program Implementation Unit hired by the African Development Bank, and the final selection is approved by the JADS Secretariat. Evaluation focuses on educational and professional excellence, commitment to home country development priorities, the quality of the statement of purpose, financial status and geographic diversity of awardees. The Bank's management decision and approval of the finalist also takes into consideration geographical diversity, gender balance, equity and inclusiveness (unusual circumstances or hardships when assessing employment experience), financial needs (applicants are financially constrained), and special consideration for applicants with special needs.
existing.best_fit: Citizens of an African Development Bank regional member country who are 35 or younger and in good health, hold a bachelor's degree or equivalent in energy, agriculture, health, environmental sustainability, engineering or a related field with an excellent academic record, and have at least one year of paid employment in their home country or another African country obtained within the past three years of completing that degree. Applicants must already be able to apply to an approved master's course at a JADS partner university, must not be enrolled in another graduate degree programme, and cannot be AfDB Group staff or a close relative of AfDB Group staff.
existing.notes: There is no separate application to the African Development Bank - "Only candidates who have been offered admission and endorsed by the university will be considered for the JADS Program", and a university admission offer alone is not a scholarship award. The scholarship "may only supplement, and does not duplicate, any other source of financial support/fellowship you might have"; finalists and awardees must inform the JADS Secretariat of other funding, and "The JADS stipend may be withdrawn completely or partially if during the scholarship period the program has evidence of additional sources of support." Deferral and renewal are not addressed on the AfDB pages. Scholars "are expected to return to their home countries and contribute to national and continental socio-economic development, using the newly acquired knowledge and skills." No clinical or field-of-practice restriction is published, but the approved master's courses are limited to energy, agriculture, health, environmental sustainability, engineering and related areas. "The scholarship only covers the duration of the graduate program or two years, whichever is less."
existing.duration: Two-year scholarship; "the scholarship only covers the duration of the graduate program or two years, whichever is less"
existing.application_period: Annual partner-university admissions cycle. As published by AfDB on 2026-10-01, the next windows relative to that date are: Ritsumeikan Asia Pacific University April-intake deadline in October 2026; Hiroshima University preliminary survey 18-29 October 2026 and application period 8-19 November 2026; Hiroshima University second course preliminary evaluation 4-8 October 2026; The University of Tokyo Schedule B application period in mid November 2026. AfDB states there is no separate application to the Bank and no central JADS window.
existing.deadline_display: The African Development Bank publishes no central JADS call opening or closing date, so there is no central deadline to quote. Applications go only through the partner universities, and the AfDB's own "List of Universities" page publishes each partner's intake and application window: Ritsumeikan Asia Pacific University - "Application Deadlines are as following: April Enrollment: October / September Enrollment: April"; Hiroshima University Graduate School of Advanced Science and Engineering - "Month of Intake: April - Preliminary Survey: Oct 18-29 - Application period: Nov 8-19 - Exam. Period: Nov 29-Dec 8" and, for its second course, "Preliminary Evaluation for Apr. Oct 4-8, Preliminary Evaluation for Oct.: Mar. 7-11, Application Period for Apr.: Nov 4-15, Application Period for Oct.: Apr. 4-22"; The University of Tokyo Graduate School of Frontier Sciences - "Month of Intake: April or October / Examination: Schedule A (application period: mid June) Schedule B (application period: mid November)"; Sophia University - "Month of Intake: September / Deadline of Application: Web entry: Mid of March ~ Early April; Application: Mid of April". Kyoto University and Kogakuin University are listed with "Please refer to the program website".
